lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: Awakening
lines.text: Good morning, Commander. We have arrived in high orbit over Kepler four forty-two b. I am EVA, your ship intelligence. The Longhaul is holding steady. Open your tablet when you are ready. There is no hurry. After all that darkness, you deserve a moment to wake up.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: A place to call home
lines.text: Tablet linked. Your quarters are still in sleep mode. Switch on the lights, then approach the private-room door and scan your handprint. This ship has carried you a long way. Let us make it feel like home again.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: The view
lines.text: Handprint verified. Welcome home, Commander. Open the thermal curtain. Those silver bands are clouds, not ice. Somewhere beneath them, an entire world is waking up. When you have had your moment, return to the pilot seat. We have a survey to finish.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: Through the fire
lines.text: Entry survey authorized. Keep your hands clear of the flight controls. I will manage the descent and deploy the thermal shades when the hull temperature rises. The noise is expected. If you can hear me, we are still together. Beginning our approach.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: A voice beneath the clouds
lines.text: Holding at sixty kilometres. Survey sensors are recording. Wait. There is a second signal beneath the atmospheric noise. It matches the missing survey vessel Kestrel. Commander, that ship was declared lost thirty-seven years ago. I have saved its coordinates. First, we need to get back into orbit.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: Containment
lines.text: Reactor containment is oscillating. I have isolated the engine room. Do not force the bulkhead. Link to the maintenance drone and seal the thermal vent, or use the remote repair controls. I can hold our altitude, but I cannot make this repair for you. Take it one step at a time.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: The missing ship
lines.text: Containment stable. We are back in orbit. I have added the Kestrel to your navigation chart. We can leave this mystery behind, or find out why it called to us. Take the pilot seat, select the wreck, and set a course. The decision to go is yours.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: What they left behind
lines.text: The Kestrel's recorder is intact. Its crew found something at the Pilgrim Vault. Not a weapon. Not a warning. A memory archive, built to survive its makers. The coordinates are in your chart. Survey the vault and recover its navigation seed. We should not let their last message disappear.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: Bring them home
lines.text: Archive secured. I can read it now. They knew their star was dying. They sent their stories outward, hoping someone would listen. We did. Return to Asterion Anchorage, dock, and carry the discoveries to the exploration exchange. Let us make sure someone else can hear them too.

lines.speaker: EVA
lines.title: A long way home
lines.text: The archive has been accepted. Their names will not be lost. Neither will the Kestrel's. When we left home, I thought our mission was to measure the distance between the stars. I was wrong. It was to find what makes that distance worth crossing. Thank you, Commander. The story is complete. The ship, and the open sky, are yours.
